relations.quote: The recursion is built on the [Three-element subset intersection construction](subset-intersection-construction.md), which gives $s<Wm$ smaller calls.

symbols.name: power exponent
symbols.meaning: The exponent, below 1, of the fixed power of the call parameter that bounds the cost per bit.
symbols.quote: Recursive power saving is the argument that a recursion's cost per bit can grow as a fixed power of its parameter, with exponent $\lambda<1$ (this letter changes meaning here: on the tensor-product page $\lambda$ is a scalar), which the main theorem needs.

symbols.name: call parameter
symbols.meaning: The parameter of a call, counting field digits for an address interchange or selected axes for a numerical layer.
symbols.quote: Let $f$ be the parameter of a call (this letter changes meaning here: on the linear-network page $f$ is the logical array): the number of field digits for an address interchange (exchanging two disjoint address fields of $u$ bits), or the number of selected axes for a numerical layer (a butterfly layer on chosen axes of a polynomial-valued array).

symbols.name: growth factor
symbols.meaning: The factor by which the call parameter grows from one call to the recursive call.
symbols.quote: Here $m$ is the factor by which the parameter grows; this letter changes meaning from the subspace dimension of the prerequisite and from the tape position on the address-fields page.

symbols.name: cost per volume
symbols.meaning: The cost of a call divided by the volume V it works on.
symbols.quote: Let $\Phi(f)$ be the cost of a call divided by the volume $V$ it works on.

symbols.name: outside-work constant
symbols.meaning: A constant bounding the call's own outside work by a multiple of (mf) to the power lambda.
symbols.quote: Let $C$ be a constant such that the call's own outside work is at most $C(mf)^\lambda$, so

symbols.name: interchange exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed exponent below 1 in the cost O(V u^tau) of an address interchange of u-bit fields.
symbols.quote: An address interchange of $u$-bit fields costs $O(Vu^\tau)$, where $\tau<1$ is fixed.

symbols.name: chunk bit count
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in one axis chunk.
symbols.quote: Here $K$ is the bit count of one axis chunk (this letter changes meaning here: on the tensor-product page $K$ is the number of factors), $d$ is the paper's axis-count parameter (this letter changes meaning from the DFT page), and $\eta>0$ is fixed, with $K\le d^\eta$.

symbols.name: axis-count parameter
symbols.meaning: The paper's parameter counting the axes of the array.
symbols.quote: Here $K$ is the bit count of one axis chunk (this letter changes meaning here: on the tensor-product page $K$ is the number of factors), $d$ is the paper's axis-count parameter (this letter changes meaning from the DFT page), and $\eta>0$ is fixed, with $K\le d^\eta$.

symbols.name: chunk exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed positive exponent with chunk bit count K at most d to the power eta.
symbols.quote: Here $K$ is the bit count of one axis chunk (this letter changes meaning here: on the tensor-product page $K$ is the number of factors), $d$ is the paper's axis-count parameter (this letter changes meaning from the DFT page), and $\eta>0$ is fixed, with $K\le d^\eta$.

symbols.name: threshold exponent
symbols.meaning: The exponent, equal to one half, in the threshold f at least d to the power beta below which the recursion stops.
symbols.quote: Since $\beta=\tfrac12$ (this letter changes meaning here: on the linear-network page $\beta$ is an edge head) and $f\ge d^\beta$ at an internal node, $d\le f^{1/\beta}$, so the outside work divided by $V$ is $O((fK)^\tau+1)\le O(f^{\tau(1+\eta/\beta)}+1)$, which is $O(f^\lambda)$ when $\lambda>\tau(1+\eta/\beta)$.

symbols.meaning: The number of levels of unrolling the recursion, so that after nu levels the weight is (s/W) to the power nu.

symbols.name: leaf exponent
symbols.meaning: An exponent at least max{0, log_m(s/W)} and below lambda, used to bound the leaf cost.
